framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Principles and playbook set a consistent approach for the UK government; organisations should also follow their own governance policies (especially security and data handling) and involve assurance teams early, with documented review and escalation processes.
who_tests: Organisation's assurance teams / AI review board

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Fully test the product before deployment, have robust assurance and regular checks of the live tool, and provide ways for users to report issues that prompt human review.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Ethics and societal impact: fairness (intro paragraph on measurements)
requirement_paraphrase: Where possible, make specific and robust measurements to assess AI systems, for example evaluating accuracy and output quality against protected characteristics in the Equality Act 2010, choosing assessments suited to the technology and use case.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: AI services must be secure and resilient and comply with Secure by Design principles and the Government Cyber Security Standard; build safeguards including security testing and, for generative AI, content filtering and validation checks.
what_is_tested: Security testing and validation of outputs

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Security > Practical recommendations (applies to generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Avoid putting LLM chatbots on public-facing government websites unless the risk of direct prompt injection is acceptable for the use case; prevent generative AI responses from automatically triggering destructive or irreversible actions without human review; review enterprise access controls before deploying AI tools.
what_is_tested: Prompt-injection risk acceptance; access-control review before deployment

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: The playbook states a data protection impact assessment is needed before implementing AI where UK GDPR Art. 35(3)(a) conditions apply, and the ICO also requires one for innovative technology processing personal data; the DPIA should cover each lifecycle stage including testing.
what_is_tested: Data protection risk assessment before deployment
who_tests: Controller (public body) with DPO; ICO guidance
document_to_download: Keep as unverified. User to read Playbook > Using AI safely and responsibly > Data protection and privacy > Lawfulness and purpose limitation (DPIA) in a browser: AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, 10 Feb 2025), HTML edition at the source_url.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Data protection and privacy > Accuracy: Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Test AI outputs against existing knowledge and expertise during training and testing; be transparent that outputs are statistically informed guesses; document sources.
document_to_download: Keep unverified. User to open Data protection and privacy > Accuracy > Practical recommendations in a browser. Note the Accuracy heading may sit under Data protection and privacy as the row states, not confirmable.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Governance > AI quality assurance (Validation of AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Any update to an AI system must go through a quantitative testing and validation process within change control; products and services should comply with relevant SDO standards such as ISO.
document_to_download: Keep unverified. User to read Using AI safely and responsibly > Governance > AI quality assurance in a browser.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Once released, keep ongoing performance monitoring with evidence that the system operates as expected; use managed release processes with the ability to withdraw and revert; monitor for model drift.
document_to_download: Keep unverified. User to read Governance > AI quality assurance (operational monitoring) in a browser.

framework: UK Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS)
requirement_paraphrase: The mandatory record applies to tools in Beta/Pilot or Production phase; records for earlier phases are optional.

framework: UK Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS)
clause_or_page: Guidance for public sector bodies, section 13 Risks, Mitigations and Impact Assessments
requirement_paraphrase: Record completed impact assessments (e.g. DPIAs; a link suffices), identified risks (data, application, efficacy, outputs, organisational, public engagement) and mitigations; update the record when substantive changes occur such as a pilot moving to production or new training data.
what_is_tested: Disclosure of impact assessments and risks

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
requirement_paraphrase: Lists a spectrum of assurance mechanisms - risk assessment, impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment (often including performance testing), formal verification - to be used in combination across the AI lifecycle, proportionate to risk.
who_tests: Internal teams or third-party assurance providers

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
requirement_paraphrase: Conformity assessment may include testing, inspection, validation, verification and certification; depending on risk it should be done by an independent third-party body; it is UK government policy that where third-party conformity assessment is sought it should come from a UKAS-accredited organisation.
who_tests: Independent third-party conformity assessment body (UKAS-accredited per policy)

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
requirement_paraphrase: States that there is not currently statutory AI regulation in the UK; systems must still meet existing law such as UK GDPR and the Equality Act 2010.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
clause_or_page: Same document, 'Criteria for selecting models' and 'A note on evaluations'
requirement_paraphrase: AISI cannot evaluate all models; selection uses estimated risk such as training compute and expected accessibility; AISI states it is not a regulator, does not designate systems 'safe', and is not responsible for release decisions of those whose systems it evaluates.
what_is_tested: Selection of models for evaluation; limits of AISI assurance

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
requirement_paraphrase: AISI states it tests leading AI systems before they are released and collaborates with AI companies, with pre-deployment access to leading models; it open-sources evaluation tools such as Inspect.
document_to_download: User to download/open by hand: UK AI Security Institute 'About' page, https://www.aisi.gov.uk/about (save as PDF, record date).

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
clause_or_page: Research Agenda (aisi.gov.uk/research-agenda), 'Our Approach' and 'Generalised effective measurement risk research'
requirement_paraphrase: AISI aims to distil findings into best practices, standards and protocols, and researches the 'science of evaluations' so that measurements of frontier capability are accurate, robust and decision-useful.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
requirement_paraphrase: Inspect is an open evaluation framework from UK AISI and Meridian Labs: an evaluation is a Task of dataset, solver and scorer; includes 200+ pre-built evaluations, agent evaluation support and sandboxing for running untrusted model code.
what_is_tested: Capabilities, agentic behaviour, reasoning, knowledge, behaviour and multimodal understanding
who_tests: Any evaluator using the open-source tool
document_to_download: User to download/open by hand: Inspect AI welcome page, https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/ (save as PDF, note version).

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Compare results with pre-defined thresholds then review failure cases; adjust thresholds only with documented evidence; break results down by sub-category and attack technique, quantify variance and confidence intervals across runs, and analyse failures qualitatively including faults in the LLM judge.
what_is_tested: Result analysis, uncertainty and judge reliability
document_to_download: Re-verify by hand from the PDF, pp.94-95. Note: ToC puts 3.7.2 on p.94 (row says 94-95); page range cannot be confirmed.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Re-test after scheduled reviews, on user feedback, and after significant changes such as a new LLM, changed system prompt, architecture or integrations; repeat original benchmarks to check safety impact.
document_to_download: Re-verify by hand from the PDF p.96. Optionally rename topic to match heading 'Continuous Monitoring and Re-testing'.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (19 June 2024)
clause_or_page: Trusted Development and Deployment dimension, 'Evaluation', p.14
requirement_paraphrase: Benchmarking and red teaming are the two main evaluation approaches today but fall short of robust assessment; the framework calls for a more systematic, comparable safety evaluation approach and suggests a baseline set of required safety tests developed with policymakers; greater transparency to government may be needed for high-risk models.
document_to_download: Download by hand: https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Model-AI-Governance-Framework-for-Generative-AI-19-June-2024.pdf (Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI, 19 June 2024) and check Evaluation p.14.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (19 June 2024)
clause_or_page: Trusted Development and Deployment dimension, 'Disclosure', p.14
requirement_paraphrase: Model developers and deployers should disclose, 'food label' style, data used, training infrastructure, an overview of evaluations done and key results, mitigations, risks and limitations, intended use and user data protection.
document_to_download: Download by hand: https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Model-AI-Governance-Framework-for-Generative-AI-19-June-2024.pdf (Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI, 19 June 2024) and check Disclosure p.14.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (19 June 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Third-party testing and assurance complements internal testing; standardise how to test (common benchmarks, tooling, later standards via ISO/IEC and IEEE) and who tests (an eventual accreditation mechanism for independent testers); robustness and fairness testing as a starting baseline.
document_to_download: Download by hand: https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Model-AI-Governance-Framework-for-Generative-AI-19-June-2024.pdf (Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI, 19 June 2024) and check Testing and Assurance p.19-20.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: p.40 case study: Google x Singapore Government sandbox
requirement_paraphrase: Case study of testing computer-use agents in a sandbox with CSA, GovTech and IMDA: use realistic data and environments, log reasoning at each step, test indirect prompt injection, keep humans in the loop during testing; found agents navigating to arbitrary URLs and including extraneous personal details in some cases.
what_is_tested: Computer-use agent behaviour for public sector use cases
document_to_download: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI v1.5 PDF (download by hand and re-check s.2.3.x case study)

framework: Singapore Cataloguing LLM Evaluations (IMDA / AI Verify Foundation discussion draft, October 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends a baseline of pre-deployment evaluations that LLMs should minimally be tested on regardless of use case: bias, factuality, toxicity generation, robustness and data governance, described as a policy position.
document_to_download: Download by hand: https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Cataloguing_LLM_Evaluations.pdf (Cataloguing LLM Evaluations discussion draft) and check Intro para 4(c) and Part 3 paras 39-42.
